name: Exact SI elementary charge e = 1.602176634e-19 C and achievable.py's hbar, c, G (G = 6.67430e-11) for the reduced Planck mass in eV

source.located: The SI-2019 definition (CGPM 2018 Res. 1; BIPM SI Brochure 9th ed. 2019) fixes e = 1.602176634e-19 C exactly from 20 May 2019; the numerical values are the CODATA 2018 recommended values (Tiesinga, Mohr, Newell, Taylor, RMP 93, 025010 (2021), no arXiv copy), unchanged for e, c, h, hbar and G in CODATA 2022 (Mohr, Newell, Taylor, Tiesinga, arXiv:2409.03787, RMP 97, 025002 (2025)). The Planck-mass convention is GMMPS's (arXiv:2604.01047 sec. 5.3).

published_statement: NIST CODATA 2018 and 2022 tables (READ): e = 1.602 176 634e-19 C (exact); c = 299 792 458 m/s (exact); h = 6.626 070 15e-34 J/Hz (exact); hbar = 1.054 571 817...e-34 J s (exact, printed with an ellipsis: the exact value is h/2pi); G = 6.674 30(15)e-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2, identical in 2018 and 2022; Planck mass energy equivalent 1.220 890(14)e19 GeV. CODATA 2014 (READ): e = 1.602 176 6208(98)e-19 C, measured. Convention (sibling-READ, GMMPS 5.3): M_P^2 = kappa^-1 = 1/(8 pi G), the reduced Planck mass.
published_hypotheses: H1 (SI 2019): e, h, c are exact by definition, not measurement, from 20 May 2019 (tables mark them '(exact)'; the 2014 table gives e with u_r 6.1e-9) -- hence J -> eV is an exact division by e
H2 (display truncation): hbar = h/2pi exactly; the table's '1.054 571 817...' is a truncated display

H3 (G is measured and carries a standard uncertainty): u(G) = 0.000 15e-11, u_r 2.2e-5; per sibling-READ 2409.03787 this is an EXPANDED uncertainty (factor 3.9) over 16 mutually inconsistent inputs, and no new G datum entered 2018-2022
H4 (a recommended value is dated): valid as of its adjustment's closing date; a later adjustment supersedes it (for these five constants 2022 changed nothing)
H5 (convention, GMMPS): the M_P in Lambda = 6 Omega alpha (m/M_P)^4 M_P^2 and in 'Lambda ~= 7.15e-121 M_P^2' is the REDUCED Planck mass sqrt(hbar c/8 pi G)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H3 (G's uncertainty and the inconsistency of its inputs): achievable.py:302 types G_SI = 6.67430e-11 with no uncertainty, and linstab.py:626 uses it as exact. Computed NOT to narrow THIS use: along the tree's path m ~ G^(-1/2), so leaving the selftest's 2% window needs dG/G = +6.4% or -1.8% (> 450 CODATA sigma); CODATA +-1 sigma moves m by 1.12e-5, a +-1e-3 envelope by 5.0e-4. (The same dropped hypothesis DOES narrow other owners' 6-11 s.f. pins -- that is the sibling entry codata-2018-constants, NARROWED -- not linstab.)
WEAKENED H2 (discrepancy, not a refutation): achievable.py:299 types HBAR = 1.054571817e-34, the truncated display, not h/2pi: -6.127e-10 relative; Mbar moves 3.06e-10.
KEPT H1: linstab.py:321-323 'EXACT by the 2019 SI definition' agrees with both tables; the division by e at linstab.py:627 converts J to eV exactly as claimed.

KEPT H5, and it is load-bearing: linstab.py:624-627 computes sqrt(hbar c/8 pi G) c^2/e, the reduced convention GMMPS state; the non-reduced mass would give m = 3.95e-2 eV (+407%) and no (convention, alpha) combination with (64 pi)^-1 enters the 2% window (non-reduced + typo: 2.97e-2).

lacked_data: Tested both ways. e: nothing can be lacked -- since SI 2019 its value is a definition of the coulomb, not a measurement; before 2019 it was measured (CODATA 2014 1.6021766208(98)e-19, READ), and the 2014 -> 2018 change, 8.24e-9 relative (1.35 x the 2014 u_r), moves nothing here. hbar and c: exact, likewise. G: the one measured input, and the one where M's hypothesis has substance in general -- no new G datum entered CODATA 2022 and the 16 inputs disagree (expansion factor 3.9; reanalyses dispute the value at 5e-5 and the uncertainty up to ~10x; sibling-READ). For THIS result the evidence is against the missing/disputed data mattering: the use (reproduce GMMPS's 2-figure m within 2%, and show (64 pi)^-1 misses by > 20%) needs G to 1.8%, and the whole dispute is < 1e-3 (computed: m moves <= 5.0e-4). The load-bearing choice is not a datum at all but the convention (reduced vs non-reduced Planck mass, factor 5.01 in m), and the tree's choice is the one GMMPS state (sibling-READ).
grade_evidence: As used at linstab.py:321-323 and 624-633 -- e exact by SI 2019 to turn J into eV, and achievable.py's hbar, c, G in the reduced-Planck-mass formula for GMMPS's 5.3 inversion -- every value equals the NIST CODATA 2018 and 2022 tables READ here (e, c, h, hbar marked exact; G 6.674 30(15)e-11 unchanged in 2022); the formula re-derives in sympy; the tree's function equals an independent re-typing bit for bit and agrees with CODATA's own Planck mass/sqrt(8 pi) to 1.05e-7; and no moved or contested datum moves the conclusion it feeds (G over +-1e-3: m moves <= 5.0e-4 against a 2% window needing >= 1.8%; pre-2019 e: 8.24e-9). The dropped G uncertainty (H3) does not narrow THIS use, computed. Discrepancies recorded, not repaired: hbar typed as the truncated display (-6.13e-10); the sibling GMMPS audit's G^(-1/4) is the physical-path exponent while the tree's code path is G^(-1/2) (both computed, both negligible). Caveat on reading: the SI definition itself and the CODATA papers were not re-read in this stage (alphaXiv quota exhausted, arxiv.org refused by the proxy); the grade rests on the NIST table text READ here, corroborated by the sibling stage's READ of arXiv:2409.03787 (8 of 8 values agree with the same table copy).
what_would_change_the_grade: OPEN if the NIST table copy in scipy were shown not to be faithful (it is corroborated against 2409.03787 by the sibling stage only). NARROWED if a later reading of GMMPS 5.3 showed their M_P is not the reduced Planck mass (the tree's 7.8e-3 reproduction would then rest on a convention the source does not use). DATA-DEPENDENT only if G moved by >= 1.8% -- no literature read suggests anything within 1e-3. Nothing about e can move it short of a redefinition of the SI.
